components.name: Chart/Map
components.description: Regional statistics on a map of Uzbekistan (14 regions). Choropleth colours each region on dataviz/sequential; Bubble keeps land neutral (dataviz/track) and sizes circles by value (area); Hex is a tile-grid map — equal-size hexes so small regions (Toshkent sh.) stay visible, labels follow CMP-07. Fixed geometry: the Map frame is centred, never stretched. Map data: svg-maps by Victor Cazanave, CC B

Design System
Chart/Map
Regional statistics on a map of Uzbekistan: Choropleth colours regions, Bubble sizes circles by value on neutral land, Hex shows every region as an equal tile. 3 variants.

When to use
Values per region where geography matters — branch coverage, users, prices, results by viloyat.
Bubble for counts (population, users): area, not colour, carries the amount.
Hex when small regions (Toshkent sh.) must stay visible and comparable.

Usage
Rules that keep the chart honest and readable.
Choropleth only for rates and shares — counts belong on Bubble.
Classed scale (5–6 steps) with the range shown in the legend.
Always pair with a ranked table or tooltip: area misleads (Qoraqalpog‘iston looks huge).
Credit the map source: svg-maps (V. Cazanave), CC BY 4.0.
Big area ≠ big value
Large regions dominate a choropleth. Use Hex or Bubble when Toshkent sh. or other small regions carry the story.
Spec
Library-neutral contract — maps to Recharts, ECharts, D3, Visx, SwiftUI Charts or Compose.
